title: In Vivo Quantitative Assessment of Myocardial Structure, Function, Perfusion and Viability Using Cardiac Micro-computed Tomography
protocol: Anesthetize the mouse by inhalation of 4% isoflurane.
Intubate the animal using a 20 G cannula.
Respirate the mouse at 100 breaths per minute with a peak inspiratory pressure of 18 cm H2O and a positive end expiratory pressure of 4 cm H2O.
Maintain anesthesia with a gas mixture of O2/N2 (v/v = 1/2) containing 2.5% isoflurane.
Apply eye drops to prevent desiccation of the eyes while under anesthesia.
Place the mouse on a heating pad and measure body temperature rectally to maintain body temperature at 37 °C during surgery.
Inject buprenorphine (0.05-0.2 mg/kg) subcutaneously just prior to surgery.
Check the toe pinch reflex to assure sufficient depth of anesthesia before starting the surgical procedure.
Depilate the mouse chest using hair removal cream.
Apply iodine to the skin.
Perform an incision by making a small cut with scissors in the skin between the 2nd and 3rd left ribs.
Pull the pectoralis minor and the xiphihumeralis muscle as well as the latissimus dorsi muscle to the side using small hooks.
Carefully cut through the 3rd intercostal muscle without harming the lungs using a curved 2 mm blade spring scissor.
Push the lung aside using a small piece of wet gauze and rupture the pericardium.
Reposition the small hooks that hold the muscle inside the thorax so that a large part of the left ventricular (LV) free wall and part of the left atrium are visible.
Insert a 7-0 silk surgical suture underneath the left coronary artery.
Occlude the artery by firmly knotting the suture.
Visually check for successful induction of the infarct by confirming the paling of the left ventricular free wall.
Perform an additional attempt to occlude the LAD if paling is not observed.
Close the chest firmly using a 6-0 silk surgical suture.
Clean the wound with saline.
Close the skin using silk sutures.
Apply wound spray on the skin to stimulate healing and prevent infection.
Turn off isoflurane and wait for animal to start breathing independently before removing ventilation tube.
Place mouse in a cage on a heating pad during recovery.
Do not leave an unattended animal until it can maintain ventral recumbency post-surgery.
Administer additional buprenorphine doses every 8-12 hours after surgery for analgesia.
Inject Buprenorphine (50 µg/kg) intraperitoneally.
Expose and treat the rubber of the vial stopper using 70% alcohol.
Withdraw a required volume (5-10 µl/g of body weight) of contrast agent with a low dead space syringe.
Purge air bubbles from the syringe by advancing the plunger back and forth or tapping gently, then expel air into sterile absorbent tissue until fluid appears at the tip.
Swab the tail with 70% alcohol prior to injection.
Warm up the tail using a lamp or warm water (40-45 °C) for vessel dilation.
Inject the contrast agent intravenously at 5-10 µl/g of body weight.
Turn on MicroCT scanner by pressing the computer power button.
Start the MicroCT control software and warm up the X-ray tube.
Allow the Live Mode button to appear in the control software indicating that warm-up is complete.
Insert the small bore cover and place the small animal bed.
Create or select the appropriate database where the image data will be saved.
Click the New Database button, enter a name for the new database, click Browse, navigate to the drive, and click OK.
Observe the new database in the Database window.
Connect to an existing database by clicking the Connect to Database button and double-clicking the database name.
Set the scan conditions by selecting 90 kV from the X-ray tube voltage drop-down menu.
Select 160 µA from the CT X-ray tube current drop-down menu.
Select 80 µA from the Live X-ray tube current drop-down menu.
Select 20 mm from the FOV drop-down menu.
Select cardio-respiratory from the Gating technique drop-down menu.
Set the Scan technique to 4.5 min.
Anesthetize the animal in an induction chamber with 4% isoflurane.
Place the animal on the scanner's animal bed using a nose cone supplying 1.5-2.0% isoflurane in air oxygen mixture.
Adjust the flow of isoflurane to achieve stable respiratory activity with ≤60 breaths per minute.
Close the instrument door by sliding it to the right to engage the safety interlock.
Turn on Live Mode by clicking the Live Mode button on the control software window.
Move the animal bed to align the mouse chest within the field of view (FOV) using the stage Z-axis control buttons.
Verify that the chest is centered within the FOV.
Position the animal inside the blue bounding box using the LEFT and RIGHT arrows on the instrument front panel.
Rotate the gantry by selecting "90" from the Rotation Control drop-down list and clicking Set.
Ensure the animal remains within the blue bounding box of the X-capture window.
Align the animal if necessary, using the UP and DOWN arrows located on the instrument front panel.
Note only the image data inside the blue bounding box shown on the X-capture window.

Resize the cardio-respiratory region of interest (ROI) with the left mouse click and by dragging the ROI edges with the mouse cursor to ensure clear visibility of the traces in the synchronization view.
Ensure that the ROI covers the diaphragm and the apical portion of the heart in all gantry positions.
Rotate the gantry 90° to confirm that the cardio-respiratory traces are still clearly visible.
Minimize time during which the animal position and cardio-respiratory ROI are adjusted to prevent unnecessary exposure to ionizing radiation.
Click the CT Scan button shown on the control software window to initialize the acquisition.
Confirm the scan by clicking the YES button in the CT Scan Confirmation Message.
Abort the scan by clicking the NO button if necessary.
Pressing the YES button will light up the red X-ray energizing indication located on the instrument.
Observe the transaxial, coronal, and sagittal views of the reconstructions in 2D Viewer software.
Review the quality of the acquired images for a few seconds.
Look for signs of animal movement caused by inadequate anesthesia.
If necessary, adjust the level of anesthesia and repeat the scan.
If structures appear doubled, with double edges, or streaks, adjust the anesthesia level.
Remove the animal from the scanner if issues are identified.
Allow the animal to fully recover from anesthesia under supervision.
Acquire an additional MicroCT scan during the metabolic phase (3 to 6 hours after contrast injection).
Load both end-diastolic and end-systolic VOX files into Analyze 12 software.
Open each loaded image with the Oblique Sections module.
Perform short-axial image reformation for both volumes.
Consider cropping images using the Subregion/pad volume function of the Image Calculator module to minimize processing time.
Maintain identical SubRegion Low and High X, Y, Z dimensions for both volumes.
Append both volumes and open with the Volume Edit module.
Adjust image intensity for better visualization if necessary.
Perform endocardial contour segmentation.
From the Semi-Automatic tab, select Object Extractor.
Set a seed point into the left ventricle (LV).
Adjust threshold values to delineate the left ventricular cavity from the myocardium.
Use automatic thresholding algorithms or the full width half max value (FWHM) for determining the threshold value.
Draw a limit along the mitral valve leaflet plane to prevent spreading to the aorta.
Click the Extract Object button to complete the segmentation of end-diastolic and end-systolic volumes.
Name the region (e.g., LV Cavity).
Save the object map to the corresponding file directory.
Perform epicardial contour segmentation.
Add a new object.
Segment the epicardial heart surface using Semi-Automatic or Manual tools.
Ensure both end-diastolic and end-systolic contours are correctly identified.
Perform manual adjustment if necessary.
Name the regions (e.g., LV Myocardium).
Save the object map to the corresponding file directory.
Open the appended volume with the Region of Interest module.
Load the corrected map.
Select both LV Cavity and LV Myocardium objects in the sample Option window.
Click the Sample Images button.
Save the log file.
Use the Radial Divider tool to subdivide the segmented volumes for regional analysis.
Compute the left ventricular stroke volume (LVSV) by subtracting the left ventricular end-systolic volume (LVESV) from the left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV).
Calculate the left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) by dividing LVSV by LVEDV and multiplying by 100%.
Compute cardiac output (CO) by multiplying LVSV by heart rate (HR).

Determine the left ventricular myocardial mass (LVMM) by subtracting the left ventricular myocardial wall volume bound by the endocardial surface (LVMVENDO) from LVMVEPI and multiplying by 1.05 g/cm³.
Divide the left ventricular myocardial mass (LVMM) by the mouse body weight (BW) to compute the left ventricular myocardial mass index (LVMMI).

Divide the left ventricular volume of infarcted myocardium (LVMVMI) by the total left ventricular myocardial volume (LVMVTOTAL), and multiply by 100% to compute the percentage of the left ventricular myocardial infarct size (%LVMIS).

Subtract the segmental left ventricular end-systolic wall diameter (LVESWD) from the segmental left ventricular end-diastolic wall diameter (LVEDWD) to compute the segmental left ventricular wall motion abnormalities (LVWM).

Subtract the segmental left ventricular end-diastolic wall thickness (LVEDWTh) from the segmental left ventricular end-systolic wall thickness (LVESWTh), divide by the segmental left ventricular end-diastolic wall thickness (LVEDWTh), and multiply by 100% to compute the segmental left ventricular wall thickening (%LVWTh).
Display the results as circumferential polar maps (Bulls eye polar plots).

Calculate the regional ejection fraction (%rEF) by subtracting the square of segmental left ventricular end-systolic wall diameter (LVESWD) from the square of segmental left ventricular end-diastolic wall diameter (LVEDWD).
Divide the result by the square of segmental left ventricular end-diastolic wall diameter (LVEDWD).
Multiply by 100% to obtain %rEF.
Convert mean intensity values into CT numbers (Hounsfield units, HU) for regional myocardial perfusion and contrast uptake presentation.
Rescale air selected from outside the animal region to -1000 HU.
Set water to 0 HU using a water-filled small radio-transparent tube.
Display converted datasets as circumferential polar maps (Bulls eye polar plots).
